qs.q: Why PANS OPS are a separate document from the Annexes?
o: The procedures are outside of the scope of the SARPS.
The procedures are too complicated for pilots to understand.
The document is not relevant to air crew.

qs.q: ARIWS stands for:
o: Automatic Runway Instrumented Weather Services.
Autonomous Runway Incursion Warning System.
Airborne Runway Instrument Warning System.

qs.q: A Control Area is:
o: Defined area of airspace in which all controlled flights are provided with an Air Traffic Service.
The confluence of airways adjacent to one or more aerodromes where ATC is provided to all air traffic.
A portion of airspace (between defined altitudes) where it has been determined that an ATC service will be provided to all IF traffic and some VFR traffic.

qs.q: The document 'Procedures for Air Navigation Services - Air Traffic Management' (PANS-ATM) is also commonly known by its ICAO document number. What is the document number?
o: Dac 8168
Doc 4444
Doc 7333

qs.q: Who is responsible for the issuing of clearance to achieve the safe and expeditious flow of a traffic to aircraft on the maneuvering area and to prevent collisions between aircraft and obstructions on the movement area?
o: The aerodrome Controller
The approach Controller
The Ground Controller

qs.q: What Annex to the Chicago Convention covers 'Facilitation'?
o: Annex 6
Annex 9
Annex 15

qs.q: What is ICAO?
o: An organization only permitted to make recommendations which are not binding on member states.
An organization of civil aviation operators, limited to 33 members.
A specialized agency related to the United Nations.

qs.q: Two aircraft are departing from a reporting point defined by an NDB. What is the minimum track separation required before one aircraft would be permitted to climb/descend through the other aircraft's level?
o: 30° and a distance of 15 nm or more.
15° and a distance of 15 km or more.
30° and a distance of 15 km or more.

qs.q: What does the structure of ICAO consists of?
o: An Assembly, Council, Secretariat, committees and commissions.
A Council; a Secretariat and committees and commissions.
A ruling council of a small number of permanent states (like the UN security council) with committees and commissions reporting to the Council.

qs.q: Trip fuel, which shall be the amount of fuel required to enable the aeroplane to fly:
o: From take-off, until landing at the destination aerodrome.
From take-off or the point of in-flight re-planning, until landing at the destination aerodrome.
From take-off, until landing at the destination aerodrome, including taxi fuel.

qs.q: When do PANS-ATM procedures absolve pilots from the responsibility for terrain avoidance?
o: Never
When under radar vectoring.
During take off and landing.

qs.q: Vitamins are essential for good night vision, therefore:
o: Pilots should take excess intake of vitamin A to improve night vision significantly.
Pilots should take balanced diet containing sufficient vitamin A)
Vitamin A deficiency does not matter, so long the pilot has adequate vitamin D intake.

qs.q: What is the relevance of the OCH for a precision approach?
o: It is the MDH if the glide path information is lost.
It is the lowest height at which a missed approach must be initiated.
It is the height at which an aircraft correctly positioned on the glide must obtain the visual minima to land.

qs.q: When converging at approximately the same altitude:
o: Balloons shall give way to hang gliders
Aeroplanes towing gliders shall give way to balloons
Balloons shall give way to gliders.

qs.q: Normal AOM RVR is 300m, Restricted AOM shall be:
qs.ex: Restricted AOM = normal + 100 ft and + 400 m.

qs.q: Enroute fIt levels are on:
o: QNE
QNH
QFE

qs.q: What is the International Aeronautical VHF Distress and Calling frequency?
You are flying in VMC and you suffer a communications failure. What are you required to do
o: Land immediately.
Continue to fly in VMC and land at the nearest suitable aerodrome.
Turn round and head back to the aerodrome of departure.

qs.q: If you are flying in IMC and you suffer a communications failure, which of the following is a correct course of action?
o: Proceed in accordance with the flight plan as filed.
Proceed in accordance with the current flight plan (the flight plan as cleared by ATC and any re-clearance subsequently obtained).
Turn around and go home.

qs.q: What are the objectives of an ATC clearance?
o: To see how accurately the pilot can read the clearance back and test if he can spot errors.
To give route and altitude specific information when different from that flight planned.
Collision avoidance and air traffic flow management.

qs.q: Capillaries:
o: Facilitate oxygen/carbon dioxide exchange.
Are the largest vessels carrying blood.
Control heart beats.

qs.q: An instrument approach has:
o: Three segments
Five segments
Six segments

qs.q: What is the principle objective of a rescue and fire fighting service?
o: To minimize the damage caused by fire.
To extinguish any with minimum delay.
To save lives.

qs.q: Ascending order of stress is:
o: Family death, divorce, marriage, mortgage.
Mortgage, marriage, family death, divorce.
Mortgage, marriage, divorce, family death.

qs.q: Who is responsible for the issue of a certificate of airworthiness?
o: ICAO
The DGCA
The authority of State of Registration.

qs.q: While facing turbulent weather, a pilot reduces speed to:
o: Avoid stalling.
Achieve better maneuorobility.
Avoid structural damage.

qs.q: Doc 4444 relates to:
o: Flight level tables.
Position reports.
All above.

qs.q: Circadian Circle represents:
o: Our level of alertness throughout the day.
Our level of competence to undertake a challenging job.
Our level of incompetence after the peak is achieved in a career.

qs.q: Someone calls you in a language you cannot understand. You indicate this by transmitting:
o: CAN NOT COMPLY
UNABLE TO COMPLY
CAN NOT

qs.q: An aircraft electing to change the conduct of its flight from IF to VFR shall, if a flight plan was submitted, notify the appropriate ATS unit specifically by transmitting:
o: Cancelling my IFR flight plan.
Cancelling my IFR flight.
Cancelling my IFR plan.

qs.q: An aircraft is flying under Instrument Flight Rules in an area where the visibility is unlimited and the sky is clear, when it totally loses radio communications. The procedure to be followed is:
o: Land on the closest appropriate aerodrome, then advise Air Traffic Services of landing.
Continue flight onto destination, complying with last received clearances then with filed flight plan.
Descend to En-route Minimum Safe Altitude and join closest airfield open to IFR operations.

qs.q: To which aircraft is a flight information service (FIS) provided?
o: Only aircraft in receipt of ATC.
All controlled flight from engine start to final shut gown.
Al aircraft in receipt of an ATC service or known to ATC which are likely to be affected by the information.

qs.q: What type of airspace is normally established at the confluence of ATS routes in the vicinity of one or more major aerodromes?
o: Terminal Control Area (TMA).
Control Zone (CTR).
Special Rules Area (SRA).

qs.q: Hypoxic hypoxia is
o: The result of low oxygen levels in the bloodstream.
The result of low hemoglobin.
An inability of the cells of the body to use the oxygen available.

qs.q: You see yellow runway edge lights, what does this mean?
o: You have run into the stop way.
They have run out of the normal colour bulbs.
You are within 600m of the end of the runway or have less then one third of the runway remaining.

qs.q: What is the Annex of the Chicago Convention that covers SAR?
o: Annex 14
Annex 12
Annex 16

qs.q: RWYCC and a description of runway surface is used for:
o: Aerplane performance calculations by Flight Crew.
Warning pilots of bad weather and imminent diversion.
Informing Operator to stop all operations till further notice.

qs.q: Obstacle light on top of a follow me vehicle will be:
o: Flashing Blue
Flashing Blue/Yellow
Flashing Yellow

qs.q: Presbyopia is also known as:
o: Short sightedness
Cross sightedness
Long sightedness

qs.q: If you are intercepted by a military aircraft over foreign territory, on what frequency should you attempt to speak to the military pilot?
o: The ATC frequency in use.
121.500MHz (the VHF distress and calling frequency).
No specific frequency. Try the lot until get contact.

qs.q: On an instrument approach to Mumbai you are IMC at FL70. Radar says set QNH 1007 and descend to 4,500 ft. The transition level is FL50. You:
o: Tell the controller you cannot accept, as you are above the transition level
Keep 1013 until FL50, then set 1007 and continue to 4,500 ft
Set 1007 immediately and report leaving FL70 for 4,500 ft
qs.ex: When cleared to descend to an altitude, set QNH as you start the descent.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an approved method of radar identification using SSR?
o: Squawk handover from another radar controller.
Track observation and position reports.
Use of the IDENT function.

qs.q: What information is contained in an AIC?
o: Major changes to Search and Rescue facilities.
Information that does not qualify for inclusion in the AIP.
A better printed version of a NOTAM.

qs.q: Who is responsible when damage is caused by an aeroplane to persons or property on the ground?
o: The Operator.
The pilot actually flying or at the controls when the incident happened.
The commander is responsible providing that no other person can be held responsible.

qs.q: ATIS is normally provided
o: To replace the FSS.
To relieve frequency congestion.
For the rapid updating weather forecasts.

qs.q: "ASDA" (Acceleration Stop Distance Available) is:
o: The length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway.
The length of the take-off run available plus the length of stopway (if stopway is provided).
The length of the runway plus the length of stopway available (if stopway provided).
